answer: One effective sybil defense is to make each agent identity expensive to forge: require every agent to lock a stake of tokens in an escrow harbor, a shared settlement pool that releases funds only after peers attest to honest work. An onyx ledger records each agent's history immutably, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero standing and must earn trust slowly, while a cipher-signed proof of completed tasks ties every action to one persistent key. Creating thousands of sock-puppets then costs real money and time, and misbehavior burns the stake, so the attack no longer pays.
